overview.description: KarnÃ¶ffel is the oldest identifiable European card game, dating back to 1426. It is a trick-taking game with a unique 'chosen suit' mechanism where certain cards have special powers. The game is historically significant as the ancestor of many modern card games including the trump mechanism.

history.origins: KarnÃ¶ffel is the oldest identifiable European card game, first mentioned in a town ordinance of NÃ¶rdlingen, Bavaria in 1426. The name likely derives from the German 'Karnickel' (rabbit) or refers to the Under (Jack) card. The game represents a crucial step in the evolution of card games, introducing the concept of a 'chosen suit' with special powers.
timeline: 1426: First documented mention in NÃ¶rdlingen, Bavaria

history.evolution: KarnÃ¶ffel was revolutionary for its time, introducing a suit with special powers that could beat cards of other suits regardless of rank. This concept evolved into the modern trump suit mechanism. The game influenced the development of Tarot, Triumph, and ultimately modern trick-taking games.
history.cultural: KarnÃ¶ffel holds immense historical significance in card game history. It was mentioned in medieval literature and church sermons (often disapprovingly). The game is now primarily of interest to historians and collectors, though it is still played by some traditional game enthusiasts.

rules.objective: Win tricks by playing higher cards or using the special powers of the KarnÃ¶ffel suit cards. Score points based on cards captured.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal 12 cards to each player
2. Determine the KarnÃ¶ffel (chosen) suit
3. The KarnÃ¶ffel suit has special powers:
   - KarnÃ¶ffel (Under/Jack of KarnÃ¶ffel): Beats all cards except the higher KarnÃ¶ffel cards
   - Higher cards in KarnÃ¶ffel suit also have special ranks
4. Non-KarnÃ¶ffel cards rank normally within their suits
5. Players must follow suit if possible
6. If unable to follow, can play any card
7. The highest card of the led suit wins, unless a KarnÃ¶ffel card is played
8. KarnÃ¶ffel cards can win tricks even when not following suit
9. Trick winner leads to next trick
10. Score based on cards captured
keyRules: The KarnÃ¶ffel suit is a 'chosen suit' with special powers
KarnÃ¶ffel cards can beat cards of other suits
The Under (Jack) of KarnÃ¶ffel is the most powerful card
Ranking within KarnÃ¶ffel suit is different from normal
No requirement to play KarnÃ¶ffel cards when unable to follow suit
Partnerships may be fixed or variable

strategy.intermediate: Count cards to track KarnÃ¶ffel distribution. Use KarnÃ¶ffel cards strategically to win key tricks. Coordinate with partner if playing in teams.
strategy.advanced: Sophisticated understanding of when to play KarnÃ¶ffel cards. Card counting for all suits. Optimal timing of special card plays. Historical variants knowledge.
tips: The KarnÃ¶ffel (Under/Jack) is your most powerful card - use it wisely
Don't waste KarnÃ¶ffel cards on low-value tricks
Remember that KarnÃ¶ffel cards can win without following suit
Track which KarnÃ¶ffel cards have been played
Consider the point value of a trick before using a KarnÃ¶ffel card

engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 32 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and eight ranks per suit (7 through Ace), created by removing all 2s through 6s from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy recognition during gameplay.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit in ascending order: 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank determines card strength and eligibility for building sequences.
